plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on upright stems, available in a vast range of colors and forms. In temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens, mid to late April is peak tulip season, and entire fields and public parks burst into color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to early May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide in temperate regions; famous displays in the Netherlands, Turkey, and the northern United States; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the 17th-century Dutch 'Tulip Mania', single bulbs sold for more than the price of a luxury canal house, making it one of the first recorded speculative bubbles.

plants.name: Prunus serrulata
plants.description: A deciduous ornamental tree covered in clouds of pink to white blossoms before or alongside new leaves. Late-blooming cultivars such as 'Kanzan' peak around late April, after the early Yoshino cherries have finished, particularly in cooler climates and higher elevations.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late spring (late April for late-flowering cultivars and northern or high-elevation areas)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely planted in Japan's northern regions such as Hokkaido, in Europe, and in North America
plants.funFact: Cherry blossoms are central to the Japanese custom of hanami, flower viewing, a tradition that goes back over a thousand years.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall subtropical tree producing masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers in panicles. In parts of South Africa such as Pretoria and in some tropical highland areas, and in certain northern-hemisphere subtropics, flowering begins in spring, while in the Southern Hemisphere autumn some trees can have sporadic flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the tropics and subtropics (varies by hemisphere; sporadic bloom around April in some regions)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in Africa, Australia, and the southern US
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because tens of thousands of these trees line its streets and carpet them in purple petals.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A bulbous woodland perennial producing nodding, bell-shaped, fragrant flowers on one side of an arching stem. Ancient woodlands in the British Isles become carpeted with blue as the bluebells reach their peak in late April.
plants.location: Native to Western Europe, especially the United Kingdom, Ireland, France, and Spain; found in ancient woodlands
plants.funFact: The United Kingdom holds around half of the world's bluebell population, and it is illegal to dig up wild bluebells there.
